notes.decision: The flanking ⲙⲏ on both sides of the chapter title, repeated as line 21 alone, is read as the Coptic numeral ⲙ̄ⲏ̄ = 48 (μ=40 + η=8), serving as the kephalaion number marker above and below the title in standard Manichaean codex format.

Translated 'the Wells' from ⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ = ⲁⲍⲙⲉ/ⲱⲱⲙⲉ 'well, cistern, pit' (Crum 480a, 525a) with intrusive Lyc. ⲓ. The chapter's content confirms: three foundational source-points spanning Deep to Height, each described as a 'root' (ⲧⲛⲟⲩⲛⲉ) of a cosmic stratum. 'Well/source/spring' fits the root-imagery; 'foundation' and 'depth' are alternative renderings.

Read as ⲁ-ⲡ-ⲧ(ⲉ)ⲥ-ⲭⲓⲥⲉ 'unto the Height,' a variant of ⲡⲧⲭⲓⲥⲉ/ⲡⲭⲥⲉ 'the Height' (already in vocabulary as upper cosmic pole). The pairing 'in the Deep, up to the Height' (ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲛ ↔ ⲭⲓⲥⲉ) is the standard cosmic vertical axis. Alternative reading as Greek σχίσις 'cleft, schism' is possible but less idiomatic.

Tentatively rendered 'those whom they have set forth/sent forth' from ⲣ̄- ('do/make') + ⲟⲩⲁⲣⲡⲧ qualitative of ⲟⲩⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'send, dispatch' — the cosmic act of sending the bound powers down. Alternatively could read as ⲣⲱⲡⲧ̄ 'cast off' (Crum 304a). Either reading fits the narrative of upper realms cast/sent down to be bound in the lower earths. Tentative.

Construed ⲡⲕⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲏⲩ as a verbal noun governing two genitive complements: 'the stripping naked of the garment and (of) the body.' The lower earth IS the place where the upper realms' garments and bodies are stripped from them — direct correspondence between the lower cosmic stratum and the act of denuding fallen powers.

Read as scribal abbreviation/truncation of ⲛⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'the worlds' followed by particle ⲙⲉⲛ — setting up the men/de-style antithesis between upper (psychic/pneumatic) and lower (somatic/fallen) worlds completed in lines 32-33.

Greek loanword πτωματικόν 'corpse-like, fallen' (from πτῶμα 'fall, corpse'), paired distinctly with σωματικόν. The doublet σωματικόν/πτωματικόν characterizes the lower worlds as both 'embodied' and 'cadaverous/fallen' — preserving the Manichaean valuation of bodies-of-the-lower-region as fallen carcasses. Translation 'corporeal' for σωματικόν, 'ptōmatic'/'fallen' for πτωματικόν.

Translated 'summons.' The lexeme is unidentified in standard glossaries but is structurally the chapter's organizing term ('first/second/third ⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ'). Best semantic match in our accumulated vocabulary is the verb ⲧⲁⲍⲙ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'summon forth' (the Lycopolitan emanative-vocative verb). 'Summons' captures the active calling-down then calling-up motion described in each instance: the cosmic Call goes out upon a class of beings, draws their substance downward, and brings it back upward. Confidence moderate.

Translated 'depth.' The form is unusual; could be Lyc. ⲙⲟⲩⲛⲍ 'form, structure' (= Sah. ⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ̄), or possibly ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fullness.' 'Depth' best fits the cosmological scenario of Life rising up out of the earth-substance — the ascent-from-below pattern dominant in this kephalaion. Confidence moderate.

Read substantivally: 'is choice (substance) of that place.' ⲥⲱⲧϥ̄ as qualitative/substantive of ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'choose, select.' Line 6 then refers back with ⲡⲥⲱⲧϥ̄ 'the chosen' as the referent from which Error is driven out.

Translated 'temples.' Distinguished here from ⲙⲡⲧⲏⲩⲉ 'heavens' (lines 10, 12, 14): ⲣ̄ⲡⲧⲏⲩⲉ = Lyc. ⲉⲣⲡⲏⲩⲉ 'temples' (plural of ⲣ̄ⲡⲉ 'temple'). The structure 'temples and dwellings and cities that exist in the heavens' (lines 13-14) confirms three distinct architectural terms within the heavenly region.

Translated 'array.' From Lyc. ⲥⲉⲡⲧⲉ (= Sah. ⲥⲟⲡⲧⲉ) 'preparation, equipment, ordered arrangement.' Used twice on this page: line 17 'array of those of heaven' and line 28 'the other array of cattle.' Translated consistently as 'array' to preserve the order/equipment register.
Translated 'lies' (qualitative). Lyc. reflex of ϣⲱⲗ 'spread, lie, sojourn.' The five worlds of flesh 'lie' upon the earth — a stative-cosmological position. Confidence moderate.

Translated 'in likenesses upon likenesses.' Reduplicated construction: ϩⲛ̄- 'in' + ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'likeness' + ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'likeness.' Per terminology rule, ⲉⲓⲛⲉ rendered uniformly as 'likeness.' Captures the intensifying-distributive sense that the powers go forth in many varied likenesses.
Translated 'wrath.' Lyc. ⲃⲗ̄ⲕⲉ = Sah. ⲃⲱⲗⲕ̄ 'anger, wrath.' Listed with desire (ⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ) and evil (ⲕⲁⲕⲓⲁ) as the moral-affective triad of vices.
Translated 'pour down.' Lyc. form related to ϣⲱⲣ 'spread' / ϣⲱⲣϣ̄ 'pour out.' Recurs four times in lines 26-27 of the descending motion: the vices 'pour down' upon men. Confidence moderate.

Read as 3pl future + verb of pouring/sending: 'they shall pour out.' Object follows in line 29: 'the Error and the scourge and the venom.' The verb ϣⲱⲁ likely = ϣⲟⲩⲟ 'pour out, empty.' Confidence moderate.

Translated 'scourge.' Coptic ϣⲛϣ 'stroke, blow, scourge' (Crum 569b) fits the toxic-violent register paired with Error and venom. Alternative readings (bond, shame) do not match the inventory of inflicted ills. Confidence moderate.
Translated 'they shall abound.' ϣⲁⲗⲩ- = Lyc. iterative/habitual 3pl prefix, + ⲣ̄-ⲍⲟⲩⲟ 'do excess, abound.' Same compound used in line 26 of the vices that 'abound in the powers.'

Translated tentatively 'is fastened ⟨and⟩ ϣⲛⲍ.' ⲉϩⲝ may be a verbal form related to ⲱϩⲝ̄/ϩⲱⲝ 'tighten, fasten, bind' (qualitative or 3pl 'they fasten'). ϣⲛⲍ remains opaque — possible candidates: ϣⲛ̄ⲍ 'examine, visit,' ϣⲏⲛ-ϥ̄ 'his tree,' or ϣⲱⲛⲉ 'sickness.' Left in Coptic in the english field with note. Confidence low.

Treated as 3sg.m perfect prefix: 'he hid' for ⲁϩⲧⲁⲃⲉⲥ. Lyc. ⲁϩ- = standard ⲁϥ- 'he (perfect).' The subject is ambiguous in the lacunose context but most likely refers back to a divine/apostolic agent named in the prior page or in the lacuna at the start of line 1.

Translated 'the powers' (plural). The article ⲧ- is unusual for a plural noun (expected ⲛ̄-), but the verb ⲉⲧⲉϣⲁϩⲥⲱⲟⲩⲍ 'which gather' takes a plural subject and the parallel construction throughout the page is plural. Possibly a Lycopolitan collective form.

Translated 'moisture' (Lycopolitan reflex of ⲗⲱϩⲙ̄ 'wet, mire, slime'). The cosmic-botanical context (life rising from earth-mires through to firmaments above) supports the wet/sap sense over 'mire' as filth. The disciples' image is hydrological-vegetative: life ascends through moisture as sap rises in plants.

Translated 'answered' tentatively. Likely Lyc orthographic reduction of ⲟⲩⲱϣⲃ 'answer' or ⲟⲩⲱⲛ '(open, declare).' The narrative formula ⲁ X ⲱⲛ̄ Y ⲡⲁϫⲉⲩ ⲁⲣⲁⲩ ϫⲉ — 'X answered Y, saying' — is standard discourse-introducer in the Kephalaia.

Translated 'in like manner' as a comparative connector linking the Wheel's rootlessness with that of the stars and zodiac. ϩⲓⲉ may be Lyc for ϩⲏ 'manner' or a comparative particle. The disciples are noting parallel cosmological structure across all three astral entities.

Translated 'they have been made lord over.' ⲭⲁⲓⲥ likely = Lyc ⲭⲱⲥ/ϫⲟⲉⲓⲥ 'lord' (already in vocab); ⲣ̄-ⲭⲁⲓⲥ = 'be lord, hold dominion.' The astral powers exercise dominion 'upon the back of' flesh and Five Trees from above without rooting in earth.

Read as Lycopolitan reflex of ⲟⲩⲱϣⲃ 'answer, respond' (= ⲡⲟⲩⲱⲍⲙⲉ in vocab). Here in passive-impersonal sense: the powers above are 'answered/responded-to' from the earth — i.e., their action elicits a response from below.

Reduplicated form of ⲥⲱⲕ 'draw, drag, suck' — 'that which draws/sucks them up.' The continuous-aspect intensive form fits the image of moisture/sap drawing the powers up through the cosmic vegetal structure.

Lyc habitual present + ϫⲡⲟ 'beget, bring forth' with 3pl object: 'they are (habitually) born/begotten in.' The astrological context (life-events governed by zodiac and natal star) confirms birth-sense.

Translated 'cast forth.' Verb of unclear root with 3pl object suffix; appears again in line 27 as ⲃⲁⲟⲥ̄ (3sg.f). The cosmological context — corpses of slain archons stretched out as the firmamental fabric — supports a verb of casting/throwing/spreading. Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲡⲱⲣϣ 'spread out' or ⲡⲁϩⲣ 'cast forth.'

Translated 'they sorted them out.' From ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'choose, select, sift' with 3pl object — referring to the messengers of the Ambassador sifting out the captive light particles. Standard Manichaean cosmogonic act.

Translated 'she was cast forth' — same root as ⲃⲁⲱⲟⲩ in line 21 but with 3sg.f object/subject suffix. Hyle 'is cast forth' from the archons in response to the Ambassador's image, paralleling earlier corpse-casting. See note on segment 20.

Translated 'she was shaken' tentatively. Verb of unclear root, possibly Lyc reflex of ⲛⲟⲩϩ/ⲛⲱϩ 'shake, sway' or ⲛⲟⲩϫ 'cast' (reflexive 'cast herself'). Narrative position between failure-to-grasp and falling supports a recoil/shake/throw verb. Could alternatively be 'she failed/was unable.'

Translated 'into three kinds.' ⲱⲁⲙⲧⲉ = Lyc 'three' (= ϣⲟⲙⲧⲉ); ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ = 'kind, division' (in accumulated vocabulary). Hyle's tripartite scattering after her failed ascent: onto the Wheel, the earth, and a third locus continuing on next page.

Tentatively rendered 'one' (Lyc. ⲟⲩⲉⲓ̈ⲉ fem. of ⲟⲩⲁ 'one'), referring back to a root mentioned at the close of the previous page. Alternative readings include a form of ⲟⲩⲱⲓⲉ 'depart, be far' but the parallel structure with line 7 (ⲕⲉⲛⲟⲩⲛⲉ 'another root') and the cosmological context of falling roots favors a referential 'one (root).'

Read ⲧϣⲣⲡ as Lyc. qualitative/passive of ⲧⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'seize, snatch, plunder' — 'they being seized by the hands of the powers.' The contrast is: not bound (ⲙⲏⲣ ⲉⲛ) to the wheel, but seized in the powers' hands while in the wheel. Alternative reading 'first/foremost' (ϣⲁⲣⲡ̄) is grammatically less clean.

ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ-ⲓⲉⲧⲛ̄ = 'show/reveal to us' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲁⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉ 'make known, reveal'), distinct from ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise.' Confirmed by parallel ⲉⲕⲁⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉⲧⲛ line 26 in the same disciples-question idiom 'reveal to us.'

Reflexive construction ⲍⲟⲩ + ⲍⲏⲧ⸗ⲟⲩ 'cast themselves' — likely Lyc. reflex of ⲛⲟⲩϫⲉ ⲙⲙⲟⲟⲩ 'cast themselves' or related throwing-verb. The abortions actively threw themselves down (in contrast to the passively-fallen root of Sin).

Read as perfect 3pl + 3pl object suffix from ⲛⲱⲃ 'yoke, join' — 'they yoked them.' Alternative readings (ⲛⲁⲃ 'lord' verbalized; ⲛⲁⲃⲧⲉ 'faith') do not fit syntax as cleanly. The yoking/joining of the abortions' fathers with earthly counterparts is consistent with Manichaean cosmology.

Per accumulated vocabulary, ⲛⲓⲁⲧⲉ = 'fathers' (Lyc. plural of ⲓⲱⲧ). Translated 'fathers of the abortions' — the heavenly progenitors of the dark offspring. Alternative 'eyes' (also in vocab) is possible but 'fathers' fits cosmological hierarchy better.

ⲥⲏⲕ as qualitative of ⲥⲱⲕ 'draw, pull' — 'drawn soul,' i.e. the soul that has been drawn upward. Alternative ⲥⲏⲕ from ⲥⲉⲉⲡⲉ 'remain' is possible but the soteriological 'drawn soul' coheres with line 32's ⲥⲁⲕⲟⲩ 'draws them' (same verb).

Translated 'in great greatness; in greatness' — emphatic doubling/intensification. The repetition is rhetorical (Mani affirms the disciples have inquired with full earnestness). ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ = ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ 'the Greatness' in glossary, here in adverbial 'with greatness.'

Read as Lyc. perfect ⲁϩ- (= ⲁⲩ-) + ⲭⲁⲗⲭ- 'mingle/twist together' (in glossary) + 3pl object suffix -ⲟⲩ. Doubled ⲗⲗ likely a scribal feature reflecting reduplication or geminate. Translated 'they mingled them' to preserve the cosmogonic intermixing semantics established in earlier kephalaia.

Read as ⲕⲁⲓⲉ 'field, low ground' (Crum 99a), giving the landscape triplet 'mountains, fields, and waters' as the inventory of cosmic loci from which the living psyche is drawn. Alternative readings (e.g. 'other things') are possible but lack contextual force.

Parsed as Lyc. modal ⲛⲁ-ϣ- 'shall be able to' + ⲱϩ (= ϣⲱⲱϩⲉ 'cease, fail') + negation ⲁⲛ. Yields 'shall not be able to cease' = 'does not cease coming up.' This preserves the Manichaean emphasis on the unceasing emanation of life from the cosmic Tree/Cross.

Greek loanword φοσσᾶτον 'fortified encampment, military camp' (Latin fossatum). Used here cosmologically of the great upper assembly to which the drawn-up life ascends. Standard Greek loanword; preserved as 'encampment.'

Lexeme unidentified. Form has appearance of a noun with 3pl possessive 'their X.' Possibly related to ⲗⲁⲡⲥ 'remnant' or a specialized cosmographic term for the residue/draught extracted in the upward conveyance. Flagged as uncertain.

ⲥⲁⲣⲏⲥ = 'south' (cf. Sah. ⲣⲏⲥ 'south'). Cosmographic designation: 'this world of the south' is the specific southern register of the cosmos in this kephalaion's geographical mapping. Translated as 'the south' to preserve the cardinal-direction semantics.
Greek loanword ἀκμήν 'still, even now, even.' Used here as an emphatic intensifier: 'even the very flesh-bodies.' Standard Coptic Greek loan.

Read as ⲧⲥⲉⲃⲟ + ⲧⲏⲛⲉ — causative of ⲥⲃⲱ 'teach' (Sah. ⲧⲥⲁⲃⲟ) + 2pl pronoun. Restored [ⲁⲓ̈] precedes, giving 'I have taught you.' Parallels the immediately preceding ⲁⲓⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲓⲉⲧⲧⲏⲛⲉ 'I have made known to you.' This revises the earlier-tentative glossary entry 'is paired-with' — context here unambiguously requires the causative-of-teaching reading. Per terminology rule, ⲥⲃⲱ = 'teaching' / ⲧⲥⲉⲃⲟ = 'teach.'

Verb of extraction. ⲁ-ⲗⲱⲭϩ̅: ⲁ- as bound infinitive + ⲗⲱⲭϩ̅ likely Lyc. for ⲱⲗⲕ̄/ⲱⲗϫ 'extract, snatch out' or related root. Followed by ⲥⲩⲗⲁ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲥ 'plunder her' (Greek συλάω). Together they describe the eschatological reaping/plundering of light from Matter — the redemptive separation. Translated 'extract' to preserve the upward-removal semantics consistent with ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise.'

Reduplicated form of ϣⲱⲡ 'consume, swallow up.' Translated 'consume them' — the self-destructive end of Matter, who turns upon her own members after being plundered. The reduplication intensifies the consumption.
